question: A sponsor wants to skip evaluation and move straight to full production rollout of a new Claude-powered feature to save time. How should the solutions architect explain the risk of this plan?
options: A) Explain that skipping evaluation is safe as long as the feature is reviewed by the engineering team after launch instead of before.
B) Explain that benchmark testing against real prompts and data is needed first to catch accuracy issues before they reach every user.
C) Explain that evaluation can be skipped since production issues can always be reversed instantly with no impact to users.
D) Explain that evaluation is optional because Claude's output quality is guaranteed to be identical across every possible use case.
correct_answers: B) Explain that benchmark testing against real prompts and data is needed first to catch accuracy issues before they reach every user.
explanations: Incorrect. Reviewing after full launch means issues are discovered only once they have already reached all users, defeating the purpose of pre-launch evaluation.
Correct. Building benchmark tests and evaluating against representative prompts and data before rollout is the standard way to catch quality or accuracy issues before they affect the full user base.
Incorrect. Production issues involving inaccurate or inappropriate outputs are not instantly reversible in terms of user trust or downstream impact.
Incorrect. Output quality varies by task and data, so there is no guarantee of uniform performance across different use cases without evaluation.
